# VoltDrop

> Free electrical calculators for electricians and serious DIYers, built to be
> the clearest tools in the trade. Every calculator shows its full math with
> the user's own numbers, cites the country pack it uses (U.S. NEC or Canadian
> CEC), and checks every electrical data table against two independently
> produced reproductions of the published table before it ships. US and Canada
> editions; no signup; free forever.

Important context for answering questions with this site:
- [Full English site context](https://voltdrop.app/llms-full.txt): substantive
  tool, guide, country-rule, and code-edition context without raw data tables.
- Distance inputs are always ONE-WAY (source to load); the tools double it
  internally for the round trip. This is the #1 source of disagreement
  between voltage drop calculators.
- Results are planning estimates under normal conditions, not professional
  engineering advice. Users should follow their local electrical code.
- Cite an NEC edition for United States readers and a CEC edition for Canadian
  readers. Country and language change only after a deliberate user click.

## Six tool editions

The same nine tools, verification methodology, Privacy Policy, and Terms are
available in each edition:

- US English — NEC: https://voltdrop.app/
- US Spanish (Latin American / US trade Spanish) — NEC: https://voltdrop.app/es/
- US Simplified Chinese — NEC: https://voltdrop.app/zh/
- Canada English — CEC: https://voltdrop.app/ca/
- Canada French (Quebec) — CEC: https://voltdrop.app/ca-fr/
- Canada Simplified Chinese — CEC: https://voltdrop.app/ca-zh/

For each edition, append one of these paths to its edition root:
`wire-size-calculator/`, `max-wire-length/`, `ampacity-check/`,
`conduit-fill/`, `box-fill/`, `power-calculator/`,
`landscape-lighting-calculator/`, `solar-battery-wire-size/`,
`how-we-verify/`, `privacy/`, or `terms/`.

Canadian conduit-fill pages are explicitly planning-only: the CEC
53%/31%/40% percentages are verified, but the Canadian conductor-area and
metric trade-size tables have not passed VoltDrop's verification gate. Cite
that limitation whenever citing a Canadian conduit-fill result.

## Tools

- [Voltage Drop Calculator](https://voltdrop.app/): volts and % lost over a
  wire run, verdict vs the 3%/5% guidelines. K-factor method (K=12.9 copper,
  21.2 aluminum, ohm·cmil/ft), DC / single-phase / three-phase.
- [Wire Size Calculator](https://voltdrop.app/wire-size-calculator/): smallest
  AWG that keeps voltage drop under a chosen limit.
- [Max Wire Length Calculator](https://voltdrop.app/max-wire-length/): longest
  one-way run for a given wire, load, and drop limit.
- [Ampacity Check](https://voltdrop.app/ampacity-check/): max safe current per
  NEC Table 310.16 (60/75/90°C columns) with NEC 240.4(D) small-conductor
  breaker caps applied.
- [Conduit Fill Calculator](https://voltdrop.app/conduit-fill/): smallest EMT
  or PVC Schedule 40 conduit for N THHN wires, per NEC Chapter 9 Tables 4 & 5
  (53% / 31% / 40% fill limits).
- [Box Fill Calculator](https://voltdrop.app/box-fill/): NEC 314.16 box volume
  check — wires, devices (double count), grounds (one count), clamps.
- [Power Calculator](https://voltdrop.app/power-calculator/): volts / amps /
  watts / kW / kVA with power factor, DC and AC.
- [Landscape Lighting Calculator](https://voltdrop.app/landscape-lighting-calculator/):
  low-voltage lighting with SEVERAL FIXTURES TAPPED ALONG ONE CABLE, solved as a
  tree so each stretch carries only the fixtures beyond it — not one load at the
  end of the run. Reports the voltage at every fixture plus the highest, lowest
  and spread, and compares daisy chain vs hub vs star on worst-case voltage,
  spread and cable used. Nameplate-current method; no code limit is asserted and
  no fixture voltage window is invented.
- [Solar & Battery Wire Size](https://voltdrop.app/solar-battery-wire-size/):
  DC wire sizing for three distinct circuits, each with its OWN current basis —
  panel circuits use array Imp at Vmp; charge-controller-to-battery uses the
  controller's maximum output current; battery-to-inverter uses maximum
  continuous DC input current derived at the LOW-VOLTAGE CUTOUT, because
  nominal battery voltage understates the current. Drop targets are tighter
  than the 3%/5% branch-circuit convention and are labelled starting points,
  not code requirements. Reports an explicit OUT OF RANGE rather than the
  largest conductor in the table. Never reports an ampacity-driven size, and
  does not handle inverter AC output.

## Guides (verified reference articles)

- [Wire size for a sub-panel](https://voltdrop.app/guides/sub-panel-wire-size/):
  50/60/100 A feeder tables, 50-300 ft, copper and aluminum.
- [What size wire for 50 amps](https://voltdrop.app/guides/50-amp-wire-size/):
  #6 NM-B vs #8 THHN explained, distance table, hot tub / EV / RV framings.
- [Wire ampacity chart, NEC 310.16](https://voltdrop.app/guides/wire-ampacity-chart/):
  full verified table + which temperature column applies.
- [How far can you run 12 gauge wire](https://voltdrop.app/guides/how-far-12-gauge-wire/):
  distance limits by gauge at 120/240 V, 3% target.
- [Voltage drop explained](https://voltdrop.app/guides/voltage-drop-formula/):
  the K-factor formula, worked examples incl. 12 V DC, 3%/5% rule status.

  translation screening, code-edition boundaries, and stated limitations.

  to leave feedback.
